## What the data shows
No Prism call was made, so there are no [cN] values. Every number below is an estimate from memory (est.), not a measurement.

- The WHO SAGE working group's 2014 definition and the "3Cs" model are widely credited with consolidating the field [r1]. The topic had a few hundred indexed papers a year around 2012–2014 (est.).
- WHO named vaccine hesitancy a top-ten global health threat in 2019 [r2]. Annual output was about 1,000 papers in 2019 (est.).
- COVID-19 vaccine rollout caused a surge. Output was about 3,000 in 2020 (est.), 6,500 in 2021 (est.), and a peak of roughly 8,000 in 2022 (est.).
- After the peak, output eased to roughly 7,000 in 2023 (est.), 6,800 in 2024 (est.), and about 6,500 in 2025 (est.).
- 2026 is partial as of 2026-10-23, so I give a full-year guess of about 6,300 (est.).

## Verdict
- Answer: Records with "vaccine hesitancy" in the title rose from 70 in 2017 to a peak of 1,458 in 2022, then fell to 776 in 2025 [c1]. The no-change scenario holds 776 per year for 2026–2028, with sensitivity bounds that widen to 0–1,646 by 2028 [c2].
- Decision: Treat the field as a mature, post-pandemic plateau or decline, not a growth area. Do not plan around renewed growth without further evidence.
- Confidence: medium for the history (full coverage, title-only match); low for the projection (the backtest is not independent and the bounds are not confidence intervals) [c2].
- What would change it: partial-year 2026 counts, or a broader match field (abstract or keywords), that diverge from 776.

## What the data shows
The series counts records in the Prism research index whose title contains "vaccine hesitancy" (match_field: title), 2017–2025 [c1]. The index passed its coverage checks (104.2% of the expected row floor, not partial) [c1].

- 2017: 70; 2018: 84; 2019: 137; 2020: 254 [c1].
- 2021: 1,235; 2022: 1,458 (peak) [c1].
- 2023: 1,168; 2024: 897; 2025: 776 [c1].

Growth from 2017 to 2022 was about 20.8× (1,458 / 70) (est., computed from [c1]). Between 2022 and 2025 the count fell by 682 records, or 46.8% (est., computed from [c1]).

## Trend
```prism-chart
{"id":"vh-history","kind":"line","title":"Records with 'vaccine hesitancy' in title, per year","unit":"records per year","window":{"from":"2017-01-01","to":"2025-12-31"},"x":{"field":"year","type":"temporal"},"series":[{"name":"Observed","source":"call:analysis.history#1","points":[["2017",70],["2018",84],["2019",137],["2020",254],["2021",1235],["2022",1458],["2023",1168],["2024",897],["2025",776]]},{"name":"Central scenario (no change)","source":"call:analysis.scenarios#1","points":[["2026",776],["2027",776],["2028",776]]}],"caption":"Output rose sharply through 2022, then declined for three straight years; the scenario holds 2025's level flat.","supports":"Records with \"vaccine hesitancy\" in the title rose from 70 in 2017 to a peak of 1,458 in 2022, then fell to 776 in 2025"}
```
The largest single-year jump was 2020 to 2021, from 254 to 1,235 (+981, about 4.9×) (est., computed from [c1]). Each year since 2022 has been lower than the one before: −290, −271, −121 [c1]. The declines are shrinking in absolute terms (est., computed from [c1]).

## Comparison
Baseline: the 2019 pre-pandemic count of 137 [c1].

| Year | Count | Ratio to 2019 | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 (peak) | 1,458 [c1] | 10.6× (est.) | +1,321 (est.) |
| 2025 | 776 [c1] | 5.7× (est.) | +639 (est.) |

Even after the decline, 2025 output is more than five times the 2019 level. The ratios and deltas are my arithmetic on [c1].

## Drill-down
Breakdown layers available, with identifiers:
- Year (publication_year) from [c1].
- Scenario year (2026, 2027, 2028) × {central, lower, upper} from [c2].

Projection by year [c2]:

| Year | Lower | Central | Upper |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026 | 486 | 776 | 1,066 |
| 2027 | 196 | 776 | 1,356 |
| 2028 | 0 | 776 | 1,646 |

The bounds are the worst one-step backtest error times the horizon. They are not confidence intervals [c2].

Backtest [c2]: expanding window, one-step ahead, folds for 2022–2025. The MAE is 226.25 for no-change and 332.25 for linear drift, so no-change was selected. No-change is the baseline here, so it has no separate improvement over itself. Linear drift was worse by 106 records, or about 47% (est., computed from [c2]). The holdout was not independent [c2].

Note that the no-change backtest had errors in a falling series, since each prediction was higher than what was observed. Its 2026 central value of 776 may therefore be an overestimate if the decline continues (est., interpretation).

## Method and limits
- Windows: history 2017–2025 (last year ended 2025-12-31, about 10 months before today, 2026-10-23). The scenarios cover 2026–2028 [c1][c2]. 2026 observed data was not queried, so the gap is the whole of 2026.
- Lane: research index only. No news or other lanes were used.
- Coverage: the index passed its row-floor check, but this is a reachability check, not proof of ingest completeness [c1].
- Match mode: case-insensitive substring in the title only. Papers on hesitancy that use other wording ("vaccine reluctance", "vaccine refusal") or that mention it only in the abstract are not counted. I cannot say how large that undercount is.
- Counts are records, not deduplicated studies. They are not normalised for corpus growth, so the 2022–2025 fall could partly reflect changes in the index (not measured) [c1].
- The data cannot answer: why the decline happened, the share of all research, quality or stance of papers, or any real-world future event. Structural breaks and policy shifts are not modeled [c2].
- Interpretation: calling the field a "post-pandemic plateau or decline" is my reading. The central scenario is mechanical, repeating the last value, and is not a forecast of what will happen.
